proposal.hypothesis: The catalog reports 10 distinct measured programs. Compact 128-thread tiling was the fastest at 0.00089008 s; compact 160-, 192-, 224-, and 256-thread variants measured about 0.000920–0.000928 s. Prior descriptions retained both CTA barriers. Keep the 128-thread CTA and 16-byte source records, but omit the trailing barrier only after the final tile, when no lane will overwrite shared memory. This tests whether removing that redundant synchronization helps; any benefit is expected to be small and is not assumed.

retained: Set block and items_per_block to 128 with 2,048 bytes of dynamic shared memory for 128 compact 16-byte source records.
Assign one target to each thread; stage sources in ascending order and handle partial source tiles and out-of-range target lanes.
Keep the barrier before consuming each tile, but omit the trailing barrier after the final tile because no subsequent tile overwrites shared memory.
